fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the street.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear branches and overgrowth above the access drive to maintain adequate overhead clearance for fire apparatus and tall emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the street frontage to make the driveway entrance visible to approaching emergency vehicles.
• Thin or cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence to create a clear path around the structure for responders on foot.
• Keep the access drive free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so emergency vehicles can reach the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance with visible posts or reflectors so responders can identify the turn-in point at night or in reduced visibility conditions.
• Identify and communicate to your local fire station that this property has a single access point with no alternative vehicle approach.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low branches that are touching or directly next to the house on all sides.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open gaps between their canopies.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the house, cutting them up to at least 10 feet from the ground.
• Clear shrubs and small plants growing under large trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so branches do not hang over or narrow the travel lane.
• Remove any shrubs or plants growing in the curved sections of the driveway where visibility is reduced.
• Keep the area directly around the house free of dead leaves, fallen branches, and accumulated plant debris.
• Thin scattered shrubs between the tree clusters and the house to reduce connected patches of plants leading toward the structure.
• Clear a path around the rear of the structure wide enough for a person to walk through without pushing through vegetation.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and any debris that could slow entry or exit.
• Remove dead wood and dry plant material from under trees in the clusters closest to the house.
• Separate shrub groupings near the house so there are visible gaps of bare ground between them.
